title: Past Time, Stories & Revision
subtitle: Short B1 revision of past time, stories and earlier unit vocabulary before the progress test.
lessonNotes: This is a revision package for the upcoming progress test.
Review past simple, past continuous, used to, time prepositions and question forms.
Consolidate earlier vocabulary; do not start a new unit.

grammar.title: Past simple and irregular verbs
grammar.rule: Use past simple for completed actions; examples include caught, brought, kept and thought.

grammar.title: Past continuous
grammar.rule: Use was/were + verb-ing for an action in progress in the past.

grammar.title: Used to
grammar.rule: Use used to + base verb for a past habit or state that has changed.

grammar.title: Time prepositions
grammar.rule: Use at, on and in accurately; no preposition after last, this, next or every.

grammar.title: Question forms
grammar.rule: Distinguish subject questions from object questions.

vocabulary.meaning: a separate area inside a train

practice.q: Choose the correct form: I ___ the bus yesterday.
Choose the correct preposition: ___ Friday morning.

reading.title: The Train to the Conference
reading.text: A traveller enters the wrong compartment by mistake, meets a fellow traveller and gains confidence before a conference.

questions.q: Why did the traveller feel nervous?

listening.title: Progress-test listening practice
listening.instructions: Use the linked B1 listening collection to practise main ideas, time words and key events.
listening.script: External listening tasks are linked in the interactive homework.

questions.q: Listen first for the main idea.

writing: Write 90–110 words about a memorable journey or meeting. Use past simple and past continuous.
Write about a past habit that has changed. Use used to and correct time expressions.
Make a short revision plan for grammar, vocabulary, listening and reading.

quiz.q: I ___ dinner when my friend called.
She used to ___ near the sea.
They ___ when the lights went out.
We do not use a preposition before:
We ___ get together after school when we were young.
